standard.title: Describe, draw and model ideas
standard.description: generate and communicate design ideas through describing, drawing or modelling, including using digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate and communicate design ideas through drawing or modelling (AC9TDEFP01). They have communicated ideas for a purpose. They have not yet labelled drawings, shown multiple views, used digital tools to communicate design ideas, or compared existing products to generate new ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate and communicate design ideas through describing, drawing or modelling — including labelled drawings with multiple views and using digital tools.

nodes.label: Generating ideas from existing products
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare and contrast features of existing products to generate new design ideas
nodes.minimum_width: Examine at least one existing product and identify at least one feature that could inform a new design idea
nodes.typical_width: Compare and contrast features of multiple existing products to develop new ideas; identify what works well and what could be different; use observations to generate at least one design idea that builds on or modifies what they have seen
wider: Compare features of several toys with movable parts — identify what makes the movement work; use this to design a new product (e.g. a puppet) with a movable part inspired by observations
Record the results from exploring design ideas (e.g. from people taste-testing a food product) — use the results to inform a revised design idea

response_modes.reason: Generating ideas from existing products requires students to reason analytically before generating — identifying which features matter and why. Without this scaffold, students copy rather than adapt, or generate ideas unconnected to what they observed. A sequence (observe → identify what works → identify what could change → generate new idea) builds design thinking rather than copying.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one feature of an existing product
Generates a design idea that connects to or builds on what was observed
nodes.hinge_reason: Without analytical observation of existing products to generate design ideas, Node 2's labelled drawings have no design rationale — students who copy rather than adapt cannot produce drawings that explain design decisions.

nodes.label: Communicating design ideas through labelled drawings and modelling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can communicate a design idea through a labelled 2D drawing or model, including showing different views and describing materials and features
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a drawing or model of a design idea that includes at least one label or description of a feature
nodes.typical_width: Produce labelled 2D drawings of design ideas using different views (top and side); describe materials and features; produce a model or drawing that someone else could understand; include dimensions or scale where appropriate
wider: Design a new environment (e.g. cubbyhouse or animal shelter) — show different views (top and side) with descriptions of materials and features for each view
Design felt finger puppets — communicate design ideas with labels showing how movable parts work; include notes about changes made to the original idea and why

response_modes.reason: Drawing with labels and showing multiple views requires spatial reasoning and drawing skills that develop through repeated practice. Students need to practise producing labelled drawings across different design contexts before the combination of views, labels and descriptions becomes fluent.

success_criteria: Produces a drawing or model that others can interpret
Includes at least one label or description of a feature or material
nodes.hinge_reason: Labelled drawings are the communication vehicle for Node 3's digital tool integration — without fluency in producing interpretable labelled drawings, there is no design idea for students to communicate using digital tools.

nodes.label: Using digital tools to communicate design ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a digital tool to communicate or record a design idea
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one digital tool to communicate or represent a design idea (e.g. take a photo, use drawing software, record an opinion about a design)
nodes.typical_width: Use digital tools alongside drawn and modelled communications — photograph work in progress, use drawing apps, record audio or video opinions about design ideas; integrate digital communication into the design process
wider: Express opinions about a design idea for felt finger puppets using audio or video — describe what they like and dislike and what changes they have made; play back and reflect
Use digital tools to record results from design experiments (e.g. taste testing) and use the recorded results to communicate a revised design decision

response_modes.reason: Digital tools are a communication medium for design ideas — not a separate activity. At this node, students must integrate digital communication with the design ideas developed in nodes 1 and 2. Integration failure looks like: using digital tools in isolation from the design process, or treating photography as separate from communicating design thinking.

success_criteria: Uses at least one digital tool to communicate a design idea
The digital output represents a design decision or idea, not just a picture of the product
